chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from al-Hasan ibn Hayy, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about the muḍiḥah in the head, whether it is like it is in the face. He said: “The muḍiḥah and the shijaj in the face and the head are equal in the diyyah, because the face is part of the head; and injuries in the body are not like they are in the head.”

key_terms.ٱلدِّيَةِ: Blood money or financial compensation due for injury.
key_terms.ٱلشِّجَاجُ: Head and face wounds classified in legal injury rulings.
key_terms.ٱلْمُوضِحَةِ: A wound that exposes the bone.
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهَ: The face, treated here as part of the head in legal classification.

ai.seo_question: Are wounds on the face and head treated the same in diyyah according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on blood money for certain wounds, stating that wounds such as the muḍiḥah and other head wounds are treated the same whether they occur on the face or the head. The reason given is that the face is considered part of the head, while injuries on the rest of the body do not follow the same ruling.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5384 - Ibn Mahbub narrated from Al-Hasan ibn Hayy, who narrated from Abu Abdullah Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), who said:

I asked Imam (as) about the muḍihah (a wound that exposes the bone) on the head - whether it is the same as on the face.
Imam (as) said: "The muḍihah and other head wounds are the same in blood money (diyyah) whether they occur on the face or the head because the face is part of the head. However, injuries on the body are not treated the same as those on the head."
